mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% for two consecutive months indicates an overheating labor market, which historically precedes recessionary signals and a negative risk premium, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE falls below 4.0% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during two consecutive quarters of GDPC1 decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a broad-based collapse in demand, amplifying recession risk and driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which typically precedes negative equity risk premia and lower earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three consecutive months of INDPRO contraction below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 4.0% combined with a federal funds rate below 2.0% for three months signals a delayed monetary policy response, which historically precedes equity market volatility and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 4.0% AND FEDFUNDS < 2.0% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL > 4.0% and FEDFUNDS < 2.0% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of more than 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) triggers a negative feedback loop in consumer spending and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE rises by more than 0.4pp in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline in both personal savings (RSAFS) and consumer spending (GDPC1) for two consecutive months signals a deterioration in household balance sheets and demand, which typically precedes negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and GDPC1 both decline for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both RSAFS and GDPC1 decline for two consecutive months.
